title: The access service's plain-text answers
description: The answers that are text, not JSON. A list is one item a line, each line ending with \n (never \r), and an empty list is an empty body, never a blank line. A signed text is one token, or an empty body. Patterns use only what JavaScript and Python regular expressions share. vectors/ holds what the real Worker answered.

roster.read_by: hpcworker's tools/grid_access.sh, which keeps the named-user entries on the lab volume's root equal to it
rules: one AccessID a line: the approvals with the grant extension, without the store reviewers' mock account

readers.read_by: hpcworker's tools/grid_access.sh, which gives each reader the lab group's read on their folders
rules: <AccessID> <folder>: one line per reader and folder, by AccessID and then folder, no repeats
a folder is under the lab storage's root, 200 characters at most; "." is the whole volume and then the reader's only line

signed.read_by: Beethoven for VS Code and its grid scripts
rules: an empty body: nothing is withdrawn

else one token, <prefix>.<payload>.<signature>: the payload is base64url (no padding) of the JSON payload; the signature is base64url of the Ed25519 signature over the ASCII text <prefix>.<payload>, by the public key the payload's kid names
the prefix is ASHLEYREV1 while KEY_PREFIX is "ashley" in wrangler.toml, BEETHOVENREV1 after it is "beethoven"; a verifier takes both

trial-key.read_by: Beethoven for VS Code's licence verifier
rules: signed as the revocation list is, with the prefix ASHLEY1 or BEETHOVEN1 as KEY_PREFIX says
the key id of a real key is the vendor's trial key ("trial"); the vectors' is "vectors", whose public key is vectors/key.json and is trusted by no real verifier
